title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. K is a complete discretely valued field with residue characteristic p. K'/K is a finite Galois extension with group G and inertia subgroup I, over which the Barsotti–Tate (BT) group M acquires good reduction. Grothendieck has built a trace homomorphism from K_BT(K;K') to Cent(I,W(k'))^G as follows. He reduces M over the closed point s' of the normalisation of K' and takes the Dieudonné module (a W(k')-module) of the reduction, on which G acts semilinearly; the trace of I on it is the 'character' of M. This is a class function on the inertia group of Gal(K̄/K) that does not depend on K'. In modern terms it is the trace of the inertial type, i.e. of inertia acting on Fontaine's D_pst of the p-adic representation T_p(M), avant la lettre.

This page.
(1) Constant type. Suppose M_{K'} is constant, i.e. T_p(M) is a locally constant p-adic sheaf (a potentially unramified Z_p-representation). Then the Dieudonné module of the reduction is W(k')⊗T_p(M) with the obvious I-action. Its trace on elements of I of order prime to p (p'-elements) is therefore the Brauer (modular) character of the F_p-representation M(o) = _pM. This is standard Brauer theory.
(2) The general question. In characteristic 0, BT groups over K are the same as Z_p-lattice Galois representations. So one asks: is the character of any M with potentially good reduction ('condition de monodromie') determined by _pM alone?
- Grothendieck's reduction: Brauer's theorem says every F_p[G]-class lifts virtually to Z_p[G]-lattices. Those lifts are étale BT groups of constant type over K'. So 'determined by _pM' would force: character of M = Brauer character of _pM on p'-elements of I.
- Counterexample: take M = Z_p(1) = μ_{p^∞}, which has good reduction. Its character is the constant 1. But I acts on μ_p through a nontrivial tame character when μ_p ⊄ K. So the answer is no.
(3) When μ_p ⊂ K. The constant and multiplicative types cause no trouble: the mod-p cyclotomic character is trivial, and a root of unity of order prime to p that is ≡1 mod p equals 1. What remains is the ind-unipotent (local-local, e.g. supersingular) case on the closed fibre.
(4) Test case. Take E1, E2 with potentially good reduction, _pE1 ≅ _pE2 and μ_p ⊂ K. Are their inertia traces φ_{E1}, φ_{E2} equal on p'-elements? These traces are computable via any T_ℓ. Only the case of Hasse invariant zero after K→K' is interesting.
(5) Margin note. This would force the character values into a ring like Z_p ∩ W(k) once μ_p ⊂ K (partly illegible).
(6) Next page. The ℓ = p analogue of Raynaud's semistability criterion: if _pA is constant, is φ = dim-type constant on p'-inertia?
errors: Logic of step (2): the Brauer-lifting detour is not needed to refute the naive claim. Z_p(1) directly gives character 1 while the Brauer character of μ_p is nontrivial on p'-inertia. The detour is only needed to show that 'determined by M(o)' is equivalent to 'equals the Brauer character of M(o)'. The page is correct as written, just roundabout.

Implicit hope that μ_p ⊂ K suffices: it fails in the local-local case in the general form Grothendieck reduced it to. Take E/Q_p with good supersingular reduction and base-change it to K = Q_p(μ_p), with e = p−1. By Serre (1972), tame inertia of Q_p acts on E[p] via the level-2 fundamental characters ω_2, ω_2^p. Restricted to I_K this becomes ω_2^{p−1}, of order p+1, which is nontrivial and of order prime to p. So on such an element the Brauer character of _pE is ζ+ζ^{-1} ≠ 2 (ζ a primitive (p+1)-th root of unity). Yet E has good reduction over K, so its character is identically 2. By Grothendieck's own Brauer-lifting argument, the character of a BT group is therefore not determined by _pM even when μ_p ⊂ K. The weaker pairwise elliptic-curve test question is not settled by this example.

ideas.what: Character of a potentially-good BT group: trace of inertia acting semilinearly, via descent data, on the Dieudonné module of the good reduction over K', viewed as a class function on inertia independent of K'
ideas.modern_name: inertial type / trace of inertia on D_pst (Weil–Deligne representation of a potentially crystalline representation)
ideas.where_published: Related ideas appear in Grothendieck's 1970 ICM talk 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux' and Montréal lectures (1974); this specific construction: unsure

ideas.what: For potentially unramified (constant-type) M, the character on p'-inertia equals the Brauer character of _pM
ideas.modern_name: Brauer characters of reductions of lattices

ideas.what: Using Brauer's virtual lifting (surjectivity of the decomposition map) to show that 'character determined by _pM' is equivalent to 'character = Brauer character of _pM'; refuted by Z_p(1)
ideas.modern_name: relation between inertial type and mod p reduction

ideas.what: Test question: do elliptic curves with isomorphic p-torsion (μ_p ⊂ K) have equal inertia traces on p'-elements? Only the supersingular-reduction case matters.
ideas.modern_name: dependence of the tame inertial type on the mod p representation (potentially Barsotti–Tate lifts of given type)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Breuil–Mézard, Kisin; Kraus for elliptic curves

ideas.what: Independence of ℓ of the inertia trace including ℓ = p via the Dieudonné module of the reduction ('comme on sait')
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-independence of the Weil–Deligne representation incl. ℓ = p for potentially good reduction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA7) for ℓ ≠ p; Fontaine/Saito-type compatibility for ℓ = p

missed.claim: Around 1969 Grothendieck defines the inertial type of a potentially good BT group crystallinely (descent data on the Dieudonné module of the reduction). He then asks whether it is controlled by the mod p representation, using Brauer lifting. This is the core of later questions on types versus mod p reductions (Breuil–Mézard, Serre weights). The link from Grothendieck's 'mysterious functor' programme to these questions is not usually drawn.
missed.quote: on peut se demander s'il n'est pas vrai en tous cas que le caractère d'un M (satisfaisant la condition de monodromie) est déterminé ainsi par la seule connaissance de M(o) = _pM
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: Grothendieck isolated the question of how the inertial type and the mod p reduction interact, and the supersingular case as the crux, well before Fontaine's D_pst.

missed.claim: Left open: the ind-unipotent case with μ_p ⊂ K, posed as the elliptic-curve test case. In the general 'determined by _pM' form it fails: a supersingular E/Q_p base-changed to Q_p(μ_p) has nontrivial Brauer character of E[p] on p'-inertia but trivial type. The pairwise elliptic-curve version is not resolved here.
missed.quote: il conviendrait alors d'examiner encore le cas où il est de type ind-unipotent sur la point fermé. Cas test: ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A concrete, checkable question about elliptic curves (equality of tame inertial traces given isomorphic p-torsion) that can now be answered with Breuil–Kisin modules or known results on Serre weights.

deep.surprise_reason: Grothendieck already uses an inertial-type notion for p-adic representations, defined crystallinely, and asks how it relates to mod p reduction via Brauer theory, about 30 years before Breuil–Mézard. The individual steps are routine and the general idea is in the spirit of his published BT programme, so it is a notable foreshadowing rather than a hidden theorem.
